spec.text: Explain the origin, progress and retreat of the Indian monsoon and discuss its impact on the Indian economy.

scenes.vo: UPSC, twenty eighteen. Geography optional, Paper One, twenty marks. Explain the origin, progress and retreat of the Indian monsoon, and discuss its impact on the Indian economy. The easy answer opens with one cause. Our own Class Eleven textbook warns against exactly that.

spec.text: Explain the origin, progress and retreat of the Indian monsoon and discuss its impact on the Indian economy.

strip.note: Sittings with a monsoon question · our count from UPSC's papers

scenes.vo: And this idea keeps coming back. In the last eleven sittings, UPSC asked about the monsoon in seven. So let's learn to write this one well. Then its cousins get easier.

spec.text: Explain the origin, progress and retreat of the Indian monsoon and discuss its impact on the Indian economy.

scenes.vo: First, read what it asks. Explain means show how and why. Discuss means weigh more than one effect. And there are four jobs: origin, progress, retreat, and the economy. Miss one, and the answer has a hole.
Start with the easy origin story. In summer, land heats faster than the sea. A low forms over the hot north-west. Moist sea air flows in, and it rains. That part is true.

lines: No single theory has fully explained the monsoon

lines.text: India: hotter in May than in July

scenes.vo: But our Class Eleven book adds a warning. No single theory has fully explained the monsoon. And the record shows why. India is hotter in May than in July, yet the heavy rain waits for July.
So scientists now picture something bigger. Near the equator sits a belt of rising air and rain. It follows the sun north each summer.
By July it lies at about twenty to twenty-five degrees north, as the monsoon trough. The monsoon is that rain belt arriving, not a giant sea breeze.
Other parts work with it. Winds from the southern Indian Ocean cross the equator and swing to the south-west.
A fast low-level jet carries them past Somalia to our west coast. High above, an easterly jet sets in.

blocks.text: The Indian monsoon is a _seasonal reversal of winds_ (Arabic mausim, 'season'). June-September brings about 75% of India's annual rain.
1. Origin: no single theory

• _Thermal concept_ (Halley, 1686): land heats faster than sea; a heat low over north-west India and a monsoon trough draw in moist sea air. • _Dynamic concept_ (Flohn, 1951): the ITCZ shifts north with the sun, to about 20-25°N in July; today's view sees the monsoon as this rain belt's seasonal migration. • Cross-equatorial flow: trades from the Mascarene High cross the equator at 40-60°E, turn south-west and ride the _Somali jet_. • _Tibetan heating_ (Koteswaram, 1958): the heated plateau builds the _Tropical Easterly Jet_ aloft. • _El Niño_ tends to weaken it.

India outline; Mascarene High south of the equator; arrows crossing the equator and bending north-east (Somali jet); Arabian Sea and Bay of Bengal branches; heat low and monsoon trough; dashed upper-air easterly jet; ITCZ line at 20-25°N in July.
blocks.label: Fig. 1: How the monsoon arrives

blocks.text: 2. Progress

• Onset: Andaman Sea about 22 May, Kerala about 1 June, often with a 'burst'. • Two branches: the Arabian Sea branch strikes the Western Ghats; the Bay branch turns up the Ganga and Brahmaputra valleys. • All India by about _8 July_ (IMD's new normal), in active spells and breaks as the trough shifts.
3. Retreat
• Withdrawal starts in north-west India about 17 September and clears most of the country by 15 October. • The winds reverse: the _north-east monsoon_ gives Tamil Nadu about 48% of its yearly rain.
4. Impact on the economy

• Farms: agriculture employs nearly half of Indians; nearly half of farming is _rain-fed_. • Food: kharif gave 46.7% of foodgrain output in 2025-26. • Drought: an all-India deficit above 10% with 20-40% of the area in drought; 2002, 2009 and 2015 were El Niño years. • Water: the above-normal 2025 monsoon raised reservoir levels (Economic Survey 2025-26). • Prices: RBI (October 2026) names the deficient monsoon as a risk to rural demand and a food-price pressure.

No single theory explains it; the newer view sees a migrating rain belt shaped by land, ocean and jets. With June-September rain down about 6% in 50 years and wet spells more intense, better forecasts (Mission Mausam) and stored water are India's insurance.

scenes.vo: Now we write. There is no word limit, so we set our own: about three hundred words in fourteen minutes. Open with one line that defines the monsoon and shows the stakes.

scenes.vo: Retreat starts in the north-west around the seventeenth of September. Most of India is clear by the fifteenth of October. Then the winds turn, and Tamil Nadu gets its north-east monsoon.

scenes.vo: The last job is the one people rush. The economy needs figures, not one line. Nearly half of Indians work in farming. Nearly half of that farming depends on rain. Kharif crops give almost half the year's grain. A good monsoon fills the reservoirs. And a weak one shows up in prices. This October, the Reserve Bank named the deficient monsoon as a pressure on food prices.

weak.text: The monsoon is caused by unequal heating of land and sea, like a big sea breeze.
weak.miss: one cause only; NCERT Class XI itself says no single theory explains it

weak.text: It covers the whole of India by 15 July.
weak.miss: the old normal; IMD's new normal is 8 July

weak.text: It retreats in October and November.
weak.miss: vague; no withdrawal dates and no north-east monsoon

weak.text: The monsoon is very important for Indian agriculture.
weak.miss: the economy demand gets one line and no figures
a mechanism question with no diagram

scenes.vo: Now put it beside the easy answer. One cause. An old date. Vague on the retreat. One line on the economy. No diagram. Both took fourteen minutes. Only one did all four jobs.

scenes.vo: And here is the payoff. The same frame answers its cousins. Twenty twenty asked for the factors behind the monsoon. Twenty twenty-two asked why it is unpredictable. Twenty nineteen asked why it is erratic. Learn the frame once. To see why the rain belt moves, watch our monsoon episode.
